title: Process and case lifecycle finalization
overview: Keep process-owned runtime resources alive across independent cases, release case-owned state at each case boundary, and finalize process resources only after their dependents have been released.
principle: Resource teardown must follow reverse dependency order. Case state is shorter-lived than process runtime state. If accelerator backend finalization fails, the runtime must retain ownership and the process lifecycle must remain active so the caller can retry instead of continuing shutdown with live backend resources.
architecture: SimuImp owns the production case and process lifecycle entry points. SimuContext coordinates case-owned state and process-owned runtime state. AccelRuntime owns the active AccelBackend. Case teardown must not finalize the process runtime; process finalization releases context-owned backend state before finalizing AccelRuntime. A failed backend Finalize leaves both runtime ownership and the process lifecycle active for retry.

verification.scope: tests/main/simu_imp_case_lifecycle_integration_test.cpp; verifies context-owned backend state is destroyed before process runtime finalization.
tests/main/simu_imp_case_lifecycle_integration_test.cpp; injects a backend finalization failure through the production SimuImp entry point and verifies retry.
tests/accel/accel_runtime_test.cpp; verifies runtime-level backend ownership retention after failed finalization.

tests/main/simu_imp_case_lifecycle_integration_test.cpp; feeds a multi-file control manifest through the production SimuImp::RunCase path, injects a parse failure in the second real parameter file after a partial read, and verifies real case teardown while process runtime remains active.

tests/main/simu_imp_case_lifecycle_integration_test.cpp; runs two production SimuImp cases in one process. The first configures distinct project, generic input/output, mesh/flow input, and mesh/flow output roots; the task records the effective roots while executing. The second omits optional roots and must resolve every root to its own case directory, proving the first case settings do not leak. Both cases also verify typed control values, database/I/O artifacts, per-case reset, and process-runtime continuity.

tests/main/simu_imp_case_lifecycle_integration_test.cpp; invokes Simulation::Run with the production full-simulation command-line shape, loads a multi-file control manifest, dispatches the registered task, checks database and I/O artifacts, and verifies process runtime finalization.

tests/main/simu_imp_case_lifecycle_integration_test.cpp; invokes Simulation::Run with a malformed second real parameter file after the first file has populated the real DataBase, then verifies public failure reporting, case rollback, project-path cleanup, and process-runtime finalization.

tests/main/simu_imp_case_lifecycle_integration_test.cpp; copies the checked-in test/grid/rae2822convert control scripts to a temporary directory, calls the production SimuContext::SetupCaseEnvironment and TeardownCase methods, checks typed values and initialization artifacts, and deliberately does not resolve or execute the Grid task. A scoped guard retries case teardown if a fatal assertion exits the test early.

proves: The production process lifecycle releases context-owned backend states before finalizing the accelerator runtime.
A failed accelerator backend finalization propagates to the caller while preserving runtime ownership and an active process lifecycle for retry.
A subsequent successful finalization completes the process lifecycle.
Each sequential production case reads its own typed control value and materializes its database and I/O path diagnostics before case-owned state is cleared.

Configured I/O roots are effective inside the first production task, and a following case with omitted roots uses its own case-relative defaults rather than inheriting the previous case project, input, or output roots.
The public Simulation::Run entry point dispatches a full case invocation through the real multi-file control reader and task registry, materializes case artifacts, and finalizes the process runtime.
A configuration failure reached through the public Simulation::Run entry point clears partially ingested case data and project bindings, reports failure, and still finalizes the process runtime.

The checked-in rae2822convert control-script set can be ingested by the production case-configuration path and torn down without executing its Grid task or writing generated files into the reference case; the test fixture also attempts case teardown on early assertion exit.
does_not_prove: Real CUDA or HIP driver shutdown behavior on physical accelerator hardware.
Multi-rank MPI teardown behavior or failures across heterogeneous ranks.
Every solver-specific resource release path or all possible exceptions during case teardown.
Physical or numerical correctness of CFD solutions.
The operating-system executable main function, multi-case CLI argument handling, or full solver execution and numerical correctness.
The referenced grid conversion inputs in rae2822convert are mutually consistent or that the Grid task succeeds; this setup-only check validates control ingestion, not grid conversion.
